title: Turn the already-enabled ADC4 analog-watchdog tampers (ITAMP7/12/13) into a live voltage-glitch detector
threat: Fault injection on the PIN gate and counter writes: pq1's only FI sensors are code redundancy and TAMP internal tampers; ITAMP7/12/13 are enabled in CR1 but no ADC is configured, so like Trezor's they 'are never triggered'. The STM32U5 has no RP2350-style glitch detector, so a VDD glitch that stays below the BOR threshold is invisible to hardware today.
proposal: Configure ADC4 (internal channels only: VREFINT, VCORE/VDDA, temperature — no bonded pins needed on the 48-pin pq1) in continuous low-power mode with tight analog-watchdog windows around the measured nominal; route AWD1/2/3 to ITAMP7/12/13 which already feed the confirmed-mode (CR3=0) tamper path and `tamp-wipe`. Characterise thresholds on silicon with the Scaffold/crowbar bench first (log-only build, record false-positive rate across temperature and USB-source swaps), then ship with `tamp-irq` so the response latency is cycles, not the 1 ms SysTick poll. Keep the secure TIM as the ADC trigger so NS cannot stop sampling.
rationale: `tamp.rs:290-307` enables ITAMP7/12/13 and writes CR3=0 (its comment still says 'we don't have data in backup SRAM', which is stale: the BHK lives in BKP0R..7R per #208); `grep -rni adc4 secure/src` finds no ADC driver, so the three tampers can never fire. Trezor's tamper.c:139-151 enables the same bits and documents them as never triggered — pq1 can go beyond parity cheaply because the plumbing already exists. ADC bandwidth is slow, so this complements (not replaces) pin-03/pin-07.
repo_evidence: secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:290-307 (ITAMP7/12/13 enabled; CR3=0; stale 'no backup SRAM data' comment)
GitHub #391 (TAMP never run on silicon), #208 (TAMP x BHK), #256 (tamp-irq flip), #248
vendor_precedent: Trezor tamper.c:139-151 enables the same ITAMP7/12/13 but configures no ADC ('never triggered'); ST AN5156 treats power/clock glitching as a typical threat. No wallet vendor documents a configured ADC4 AWD glitch detector.
risks: False positives under confirmed mode wipe the device (CR3=0 erases BKPxR including the loaded BHK, and tamp-wipe arms the page-125 wipe); thresholds must be characterised on every board revision and across USB sources, and #391/#208 (TAMP never silicon-tested; ITAMP6 trips on probe attach at RDP>0) must close first. A glitcher who knows the AWD window can shape the pulse below it; this raises cost, it is not a guarantee.
